<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8d1f7ab78545dea1b46a0bab064676950007b815` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

git fetch origin 8b7839919629a71fdd1a5dc6d8634b408ac9117f && git checkout 8b7839919629a71fdd1a5dc6d8634b408ac9117f

git fetch origin 8d1f7ab78545dea1b46a0bab064676950007b815 955d5a5ce8b1300373a8f1256fb2ec41d20f5621 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8d1f7ab78545dea1b46a0bab064676950007b815 && git merge --no-ff 955d5a5ce8b1300373a8f1256fb2ec41d20f5621

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8d1f7ab78545dea1b46a0bab064676950007b815` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `955d5a5ce8b1300373a8f1256fb2ec41d20f5621`

### ① Derived judgments

- **"Who was exposed: a signed-in member who does not hold the set (and listed for them)."** Base `fetchAudienceBooks` returned `[]` on fault, so `anyPermissionSetAudience([])` is false and `allReadable = caller.authenticated && !gated` (packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts `resolveDocsAudience`, head :3010-3012) admits every authenticated caller on both the list (`filtered = list`, :6633-6636) and the single read (`allowed = true`, :7602). Anonymous stays denied: `audienceAllows` returns false for a non-public audience when `!caller.authenticated` (packages/spec/src/system/book.zod.ts:434-437), and an empty corpus resolves to `'org'` (`docAudienceAllows`, :496-499), so 401 held. **Correct.**
- **"An empty corpus means 'no book claims this doc', so `org`."** `docAudienceAllows(undefined | [], caller)` falls to `audienceAllows('org', caller)` (book.zod.ts:499). **Correct.**
- **"Now the fault is answered through the route's error door."** Diff: `fetchAudienceBooks` now `if ('fault' in read) throw read.fault;` (:2979-2983) and the corpus read `if ('fault' in read) throw read.fault;` (:7605-7607); both callers sit inside the handlers' `try` whose `catch` is `handleRouteError(res, error)` (:6735, :7717). **Correct.**
- **"The same answer `GET /meta/book/:name/tree` has always given when its own book read fails."** The tree door reads books with a bare `norm(await prot.getMetaItems(booksRequest))` before any gate, inside the same `handleRouteError` try (head :6984-6990/:7040; merge-base 16c5a33f :6964); the same bare await is present in the API-fetched revisions at 2026-07-31 (`a1b61e01`, :3093-3097) and 2026-06-18 (`fd070277`, :2051-2055). **Correct** across every revision inspected.
- **"The three docs reads answer one fault one way / 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE with metadata-protocol."** `metadataStoreUnavailableError` sets `code = 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE'`, `status = 503` (packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:2845-2855; `getMetaItems` throws it via `metadataReadFailureError` for every non-unprovisioned read failure, :2894-2901). `resolveErrorResponse`'s 5xx arm keeps a declared code via `thrownCodeFields` (packages/rest/src/error-response.ts, arm at `if (error.status >= 500)` in the 2181-2330 block); the list door's own doc read is a bare `await p.getMetaItems(listRequest)` (:6372). The new test's starred case pins all three doors at `{503, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE}`. **Correct.**
- **"Healthy reads answer exactly as before."** Both hunks change only the `'fault' in read` branch; the `read.items` path is byte-identical, and the single read's 401/403 `sendDeclaredFault` arms (:7610-7617) are untouched. The controls suite pins holder 200, non-holder 403 + pruned list, anonymous 401. **Correct.** Precision note: the parenthetical "(200 / 403 / 401)" describes the single read; the list door answers a non-holder or anonymous caller 200 with a filtered set, never 403/401. Not false as a statement about the single read; not a wire change.
- **"Nothing to change in your metadata or your clients."** No `packages/spec` or metadata-shape edit; no export or config key touched (private methods only); the codes were already emitted by these routes (list's own 503, tree's 503). The next sentence discloses the one observable delta. **Correct.**
- **No new error code / wire shape.** `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and `INTERNAL_ERROR` are `StandardErrorCode` members (packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts:110,113; `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap` 500/503 at :181,184; ledger packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts:1428). The body is the existing flat `handleRouteError` envelope. **Correct.**
- **Narrows, does not widen.** A formerly 200 answer on a defective path becomes 5xx; no accepted set, published payload key or route is added. `Clause-②: no` is well-formed under .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/execution-duties.md:96-99 (runtime permission/security behaviour is the stated negative boundary of clause ②). **Correct.**
- **"No hand-written `content/docs/**` line is made false."** `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx:325-330` states only healthy gating (401 anonymous, 403 missing set, union audience) — still true; `content/docs/api/metadata-api.mdx:37` "Listing applies the ADR-0046 §6.7 audience gate" — still true; the drift bot's two flagged pages (`content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`, `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx`) name the tree route only and state no fault behaviour. No page says what a read answers when a gate input cannot be read, so nothing needed touching. **Correct.**
- **ADR-0046 §6.7 alignment.** "Gating is enforced at the read layer" — the fix makes the gate's inputs fail closed at the read layer; the anonymous umbrella exemption (§6.7 amendment) is unchanged: the handler's audience gate remains the authorization. **Correct.**

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/rest` (17.4.0) is **correct**. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3: a bug fix in a released package takes `patch`; the `(narrowing)` is BREAKING rule attaches to a `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` declaration on a published contract face, and this PR declares `Clause-②: no`, which execution-duties.md:98 supports for a runtime security behaviour change. The 200-to-503 (authenticated) and 401-to-503 (anonymous) deltas occur only on the fail-open defect path, use codes the same routes already emit, and touch no export, schema, key or route; no ADR-0087 marker is required for a non-breaking changeset, and `Check Changeset` (which runs `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration`) is green. Precedent in the released packages/rest/CHANGELOG.md: `919beca` (17.4.0 Patch, "REST no longer reads a FAILED authorization-input lookup as 'this check does not apply'") and the 17.3.0 Patch entry that turned the authz-store outage's 401 disguise into 503 both shipped as `patch`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Propagate instead of prune (deviation from triage's "prunes it from the list").** Answered: with the books unreadable the gate can clear no doc (any doc may be claimed by a set-gated book and `public` only comes from a book), so a prune is an empty list for every caller — an invented "no docs" answer; the app-nav arm prunes only because its response is a composite whose remainder is still served (`resolveNavDocAudience` docblock :3942-3954). Propagation matches ADR-0110 D3 ("an availability failure is not an authorization decision: 503") and the tree door. Accepted; the triage note was an execution suggestion and the claim comment assigned this exact response-shape judgment to the dev.
- **Propagate instead of 403.** Answered: 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` states a verdict the gate never reached and makes an outage indistinguishable from a denial (ADR-0110 D3 miss-vs-outage); the pin test asserts no 403-for-holder. Accepted.
- **Anonymous caller during a book fault now gets 503 instead of 401.** Answered: identical to what the tree door has answered anonymous callers at every inspected revision; the 5xx arm withholds prose, so only "store unavailable" is disclosed; the changeset covers it under "no doc is served or listed" and the PR body states it explicitly. Accepted.
- **Cost: holders and `org` docs also 503 while the book store faults.** Stated in the changeset; it is the fail-closed price ADR-0049 asks for and is pinned by the "no doc is cleared without the books" case. Accepted.
- **A producer-marked `sys_metadata` hook refusal is not a 503.** `metadataReadFailureError` routes a marked refusal to its own category (protocol.ts:2894-2900). The changeset scopes its "503" to "a metadata-store fault", so it is not false; the PR body records the other limb. Accepted.
- **Changeset parenthetical on healthy answers is single-read-shaped** (list answers 200 filtered, never 403/401). The primary claim "exactly as before" is true and pinned; wording nicety only, not a required change.
- **Out-of-scope side doors** (`/layers`, `?layers=true`, `/published`) serve a set-gated body with healthy reads — disclosed in the PR body as a separate class (gate absent, not fault-as-absent) for the #20130 family; not this card's scope, and not a reason to hold this fix.
- **CI at review time:** 30 success, 3 skipped, 0 failed, 1 still running (`Lint & Repo Gates`); PR is draft with `mergeable_state: blocked`. Landing waits on that run and on the record this review supplies; no contract finding depends on it.
